papers.summary: We prove that the set $\mathcal{N}_N$ of ReLU networks with one hidden layer and at most $N\in\mathbb N$ neurons is weakly closed in $W^{1,p}(Ω)$, for a bounded connected open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^d$. Consequently, every coercive, weakly lower semicontinuous energy on this space attains its minimum over $\mathcal{N}_N$. This covers the Deep Ritz method with convex integrands, Sobolev training and Lipschitz learning. Moreover, as the weight decay parameter tends to zero, minimizers of the regularized problem converge, up to subsequences, to minimizers with minimal parameter norm. We also prove that the set of ReLU networks with two hidden layers of bounded widths is not closed in $W^{1,p}(Ω)$ or in $C(\overlineΩ)$. This disproves a conjecture of Petersen, Raslan and Voigtlaender.
papers.title: On the (non-)closedness of the set of ReLU networks

papers.summary: In this study, we present a comparison of iterative methods for the compressible Reynolds equation with Navier slip boundary conditions, based on a fully compressible cavitation model for lubricated bearings. We establish the existence and uniqueness of the solution to the two-dimensional problem. We introduce the Kirchhoff transformation to reformulate the nonlinear density-pressure relationship into a quasi-linear problem. We develop an efficient numerical approach to solve the two-dimensional nonlinear problem. The methods examined are the Gauss-Seidel method, the Newton-Raphson method and parallelized nonlinear Jacobi method, applied to one- and two-dimensional slider bearing configurations. The overall solution time is shown to depend strongly on the choice of method.
papers.title: Efficient iterative methods for the nonlinear compressible Reynolds equation with Navier slip boundary condition

papers.summary: In this paper, first we study the deformations, stability and rigidity of Lie triple system morphisms by means of higher derived brackets and augmented Yamaguti cohomology. The vanishing of the first cohomology gives formal and local inner rigidity. The vanishing of the second cohomology removes the formal extension obstructions and, in finite dimension over $\mathbb{R}$, gives local smoothness and stability under simultaneous perturbations of the two products. Next, we establish the relationship with Lie algebra homomorphisms in each part of the theory. The universal enveloping Lie algebra identifies a Lie triple morphism with a grading-preserving Lie homomorphism. We obtain the corresponding first cohomology isomorphism, the equivalence of formal and smooth deformations, and a stability result for graded Lie bracket perturbations. For Lie triple products induced by binary Lie brackets, we construct a comparison of differentials and obstruction classes. Under perfectness and a zero-centralizer condition, the local morphism spaces coincide. Finally, we relate triple subsystem graphs to graded Lie subalgebra graphs and compare their normal differentials.
papers.title: Deformations and Local Geometry of Lie Triple System Morphisms

papers.summary: In this work, we propose a mass-lumped finite element method for the Allen-Cahn equation that incorporates nonlinear mobility which may degenerate. The spatial approximation uses continuous, piecewise linear, mass-lumped finite elements, while convex splitting is employed for the double-well potential in time. Under the standard non-obtuse mesh condition, it is shown that the resulting fully discrete method preserves the maximum-bound principle unconditionally: if the initial approximation takes values in $[-1, 1]$, then so does the numerical solution at every time level. Additionally, the method dissipates the original discrete Ginzburg-Landau energy without any time-step restriction, even when the mobility vanishes at pure phases. This analysis relies on the monotonicity of the lumped finite element operator and the convexity of the split potential. Numerical experiments confirm these theoretical properties and demonstrate the robustness of the method in phase-separation dynamics involving degenerate mobility.
papers.title: Mass-lumped finite elements with maximum-bound preservation and original-energy dissipation for the degenerate-mobility Allen-Cahn equation

papers.summary: We develop a conforming virtual element framework for differential forms on general polytopal meshes in arbitrary dimension and at arbitrary order. Recursive local Hodge-Laplace boundary value problems define a trimmed virtual de Rham complex, from which moment constraints yield a complete subcomplex. The local spaces of these two complexes contain the trimmed and complete polynomial spaces of differential forms, respectively, and admit unisolvent degrees of freedom and computable polynomial projections. The canonical interpolants commute with the exterior derivative, and both complexes have cohomology isomorphic to that of the continuous de Rham complex. For both virtual families, we establish negative-norm inverse estimates and mesh-uniform norm equivalences in all form degrees. We further derive canonical interpolation error bounds and discrete Poincar'e inequalities. As an application, we obtain an inf-sup stable mixed Hodge-Laplace method with harmonic variables and optimal-order convergence under sufficient regularity. Moreover, the two conforming complexes are cochain isomorphic to their fully discrete counterparts (J. Eur. Math. Soc., 2025, doi:10.4171/JEMS/1602), and the norm equivalences provide a key analytical bridge between the conforming and fully discrete formulations.
papers.title: A virtual element exterior calculus framework

papers.summary: We construct a family of division ring extensions and compute their left and right dimensions. In characteristic zero, we obtain a counterexample to the pure semisimplicity conjecture: a hereditary right pure semisimple ring of infinite representation type. For each prime $p\ge3$, we construct in characteristic $p$ a hereditary artinian ring of finite representation type with Coxeter diagram $I_2(p+2)$.
papers.title: Division ring extensions and a counterexample to the pure semisimplicity conjecture

papers.summary: We propose an algorithm for estimating the Cholesky factorization of positive, semi-definite matrices without pivoting. Our method has the same data access pattern as the canonical Cholesky method, and therefore is amenable to familiar hardware optimization techniques. Our method interprets the factorization task as a variational problem and in turn solves it using an induced dynamical system. We study the rate of convergence of this dynamical system to its stationary state for both positive definite and semi-definite matrices. Numerical experiments validate that our method is competitive with pivoted Cholesky on several practical examples.
papers.title: Finite-time Cholesky Factorization

papers.summary: In this paper we focus on rigidity in descriptive set theory. Building on cocycle superrigidity results of Popa, Furman and Ioana, we prove rigidity in the purely Borel context for the orbit equivalence relations arising from the shift actions and translation actions of lattices in semisimple Lie groups with higher rank. Our results sharpen work of Adams and Kechris.
papers.title: Borel rigidity for higher rank lattices

papers.summary: We establish a canonical topological lifting of Mundici equivalence, representing every topological MV-algebra as the unit interval of a topological $\ell$-group and extending the correspondence to a categorical adjunction. As applications, we give a direct group-theoretic proof of the equivalence of $T_0$ and $T_{3\frac12}$ and show that every topological MV-algebra is a retral space. We further extend the lifting to topological Riesz MV-algebras and identify the canonical topology with Wiweger's mixed topology under suitable assumptions, recovering the strict topology as a special case. Finally, we obtain a unit-interval formulation of Koopman representations for continuous-time dynamical systems.
papers.title: Topological Mundici Adjunction and Its Applications

papers.summary: The definition of algebraic entropy presents a difficulty in the general setting of filtered algebras, which makes it necessary to distinguish between filtered algebras and finitely filtered algebras. While algebraic entropy is well defined in the finitely filtered case, extending this notion to arbitrary filtered algebras is not immediate. To address this issue, we realize a filtered algebra as the limit of a strict direct system of finitely filtered algebras and define its entropy as the supremum of the entropies of the algebras in the system. This extension is consistent with the original definition, when the algebra is finitely filtered, the extended entropy agrees with its algebraic entropy. This new setting allows us to extend the definition of the algebraic entropy to path and Leavitt path algebras of infinite graphs.
papers.title: An extension of the notion of algebraic entropy

papers.summary: In this paper we continue the work started in [Bonzio & Zamperlin 2025] by investigating the algebraic semantics for modal external weak Kleene logics. In order to do so we study the global modal logics associated with the three-valued Kripke models introduced in the previous article, showing how these systems are algebraizable. We proceed by defining their algebraic counterparts, obtaining the classes of modal Bochvar and modal Halldén algebras, whose structure theory we investigate via Płonka sum decomposition. Of particular interested is the interaction of the modal operator with the homorphisms of the Płonka decomposition. These results allow us to prove representation theorems for these expanded modal algebras in the style of the Jónsson-Tarski representation for Boolean algebras with operators. As a consequence, we also obtain algebraic semnatics for the local modal logics from which the work originated.
papers.title: Modal weak Kleene logics: algebraic semantics and Jónsson-Tarski representation

papers.summary: We characterise the two-step nilpotent varieties of algebras: the semi-abelian varieties in which all ternary cosmash products vanish. Just as abelian varieties are the categories of modules over a ring, two-step nilpotent varieties are exactly the categories of modules over a square ring in the sense of Baues, Hartl and Pirashvili. We construct the square ring explicitly from the full subcategory on the free algebras on one and two generators, and give complete proofs. As consequences we obtain a description of any two-step nilpotent variety by generators and relations, an intrinsic characterisation in terms of quadratic term operations, and an account of its abelian core and of the lower central series of its objects in terms of the square ring. Along the way, we associate with any commutative ring $R$ a square ring whose modules, the two-step nilpotent $R$-groups, extend Hall's nilpotent $R$-groups of class two from $2$-binomial rings to arbitrary rings of coefficients.
papers.title: Two-step nilpotent varieties as categories of modules over a square ring

papers.summary: We determine the sharp constant in the weighted $L^2$ Bernstein inequality for coordinate derivatives on the unit ball with a Jacobi weight and the strengthened derivative factors introduced by Beberok and Xu. The constant is expressed in terms of the largest zeros of Jacobi polynomials, and all extremal polynomials are characterized explicitly. The proof uses an orthogonal polynomial decomposition that gives diagonal formulas for both the squared norm and the weighted derivative integral. We also obtain two-sided bounds for the sharp constant and determine its leading asymptotic behavior as the polynomial degree tends to infinity.
papers.title: A sharp weighted $L^2$ Bernstein inequality for partial derivatives on the unit ball

papers.summary: This paper presents a formalization for a theory of constructing real numbers using concepts related to filters. The formalization is implemented using the Coq proof assistant and is grounded in axiomatic set theory. The theory encompasses various notions such as filters, ultrafilters, principal ultrafilters, and arithmetical ultrafilters. A special filter, namely the non-principal arithmetical ultrafilter, whose existence requires the Continuum Hypothesis to be proven, is employed to establish several non-standard number sets: *N, *Z and *Q. The set of real numbers, R, is subsequently derived by equivalently classifying a specific subset of *Q. The entire theory is thoroughly formalized, with each detail verified to ensure rigor and precision. This work contributes a new selection of foundational materials for the formalization of mathematical theories.
papers.title: Formalization of Filter-Method Construction for Real Numbers in Coq

papers.summary: Walsh analysis connects ordered Fourier convergence, summability, nonlinear approximation, and universal representation through a common character algebra. This survey examines developments from 2000-2026 against their classical foundations. Binary kernel geometry explains Hardy-space losses and summability thresholds; interval and packet methods control spectral selection; localized blocks produce correction and universal representations with distinct coefficient and exceptional-set requirements. Selected proofs and counterexamples compare these mechanisms and identify where an implication needs an additional hypothesis. The same distinctions organize digital integration, sparse measurements, Boolean spectra, and generalized Walsh bases. Quantitative thresholds, source conventions, and published theorem pointers are collected in comparative tables. The concluding problems separate source-listed questions, proposed refinements, and elementary obstructions. Supplementary derivations preserve normalization checks and finite covariance calculations while keeping the main exposition focused on the analytic mechanisms.
papers.title: Walsh Analysis in the Twenty-First Century: Convergence, Summability, Nonlinear Approximation, Universality, and Digital Applications

papers.summary: The Stone-Weierstrass theorem obtains every continuous function on a compact space as a uniform limit of functions built from a separating family by finitely many operations, and Reggio proved the theorem equivalent to the Beth definability property of an infinitary equational logic. We extend both results beyond compactness: on every separable metric space, and in particular on every Polish space, every bounded uniformly continuous function is a uniform limit of functions built from countably many bounded separating functions by the connectives of infinitary real-valued logic, and an approximate Beth property of this logic is equivalent to the new theorem. The extension rests on a rule of syntax, which admits a countable supremum when its terms share an a priori bound and thereby makes the sentences define exactly the bounded Lipschitz functions, and on a model existence game that does the work of compactness in the proof of interpolation.
papers.title: A Stone-Weierstrass Theorem for Polish Spaces, Given by Logic

papers.summary: We study Liouville transforms for the differential equation $Ju'+qu=wf$ on the real interval $(a,b)$ where $J$ is a constant, invertible, skew-hermitian matrix and $q$ and $w$ are matrices whose entries are distributions of order $0$ with $q$ Hermitian and $w$ non-negative. In particular, we examine their use in the treatment of quasi-regular endpoints and their impact on the Weyl-Titchmarsh $\mathbb M$-function associated with the differential equation.
papers.title: Liouville transforms for ordinary differential equations with distributional coefficients

papers.summary: We study weighted endpoint estimates for the centered fractional maximal operator on the infinite rooted $k$-ary tree, $T$. Our first result is a Fefferman--Stein type estimate \[ w\bigl(\{M_αf>λ\}\bigr) \lesssim_{α,s} \frac1λ\sum_{x\in T}|f(x)|M_{α,s}w(x), \qquad s>1, \] with a constant independent of the branching parameter $k$. Although the proof is inspired by the non-fractional argument of Ombrosi, Rivera-Ríos and Safe in \cite{ORRS}, the fractional normalization introduces a genuinely new scale interaction. At radius $r$, one must renormalize the function by $k^{rα}$ while keeping the dyadic cutoff at $k^r$; this leads to a new summation mechanism involving simultaneously $k^{rα}$ and $k^{r(1-α)}$. We then study sharpness and the geometry of admissible weights. We construct counterexamples showing that the estimate cannot in general be reduced to $s=1$ for any $0<α<1$. In the subcritical range $0<α<1/2$, we characterize power-type radial weights satisfying the natural fractional $A_1$ condition and prove that the failure persists after any fixed finite number of iterations of $M_α$. We also prove that $M_αw\lesssim w$ is necessary for the corresponding weighted weak type estimate but is not sufficient in the subcritical range. Finally, we identify a phase transition: for $1/2\leα<1$ no nonzero global weight can satisfy $M_αw\lesssim w$.
papers.title: Fractional Fefferman--Stein inequalities on infinite rooted $k$-ary trees
